utterances.text: [Interpretation] My one last question, General. You said that you haven't seen documents relating to the buses prior to the 12th of July. My question is: Have you seen documents, prior to the 12th of July, which make mention of the evacuation? Perhaps all the documents would need to be reviewed. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS RICHARD DANNATT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm pausing because I'm thinking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, General. Let me retrace my steps a little because buses are one thing and to talk more generally of a plan for the evacuation of the population is another. Maybe we have a defined objective, and then we have to consider the means to achieve it. So I don't know if by making such a distinction that could assist you in refreshing your memory.

utterances.speaker: FRANCIS RICHARD DANNATT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've certainly made reference to the fact that one has seen the general stated intention going right back to the Karadzic order that to remove the Muslim population as a long-term aim from Srebrenica was in mind. That is one thing. I don't think I can recall seeing a particular written order prior to the 12th of July. And those orders largely pertain to the gathering together of buses and so on for the purpose of moving the people. So I think I can safely say that my understanding is that there always was an intention to remove the Muslim people from Srebrenica when at some point in the future the opportunity presented itself. I think that opportunity presented itself after the town had been captured, in a military sense, and that's when one begins to see written orders and transcripts of conversations and so on, gathering together buses for that purpose. And I think the 12th of July is about the cut-off date or about the start date for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, General, I think we have come to the end of your testimony. We have made every effort to release you today. I should also like to take advantage of the opportunity to thank all the staff members for their availability and readiness to continue late which, after all, was not necessary. But I wish to thank you too very much, General, for coming and answering questions from the Prosecution and the Defence and the Judges, and we wish you every success in your future work. I will now ask the usher to accompany General Dannatt out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was going to raise the question of documents. Perhaps I should also take a few minutes to address some questions. We have come against a concrete difficulty, and that is that Mr. McCloskey has asked for the admission into evidence of the list of documents contained in Exhibit 394, specifically that exhibit was tendered and requested to be admitted under seal because the list contains documents under seal. So that brought about this specific difficulty as to finding out which of the specific documents which need to be admitted under seal and which are the documents that can be admitted normally. So I don't know whether the Prosecutor is ready to answer this question or perhaps we can deal with it at some other time, because it was not clear for me, during the discussion, whether the Defence took a position only regarding the documents under seal. As you remember, the Defence had an objection regarding the admission of certain documents, but in my understanding, it did not state an opinion regarding the request of admitting certain documents under seal. Those are the questions that we still have to deal with before ruling. Mr. Harmon, please. Then I'll give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President and Your Honours, counsel. The situation in respect of the exhibits, many are under seal, many are not under seal, we have duplicate documents finding themselves in both situations, it's, frankly, very confusing. In order to resolve this issue, my proposal to the Trial Chamber is that Ms. Keith has been working on a comprehensive list of documents and exhibits and is prepared tomorrow to present to the registrar the list of documents for which we are seeking a removal from the protection of the seal and the identity of documents which we believe should remain under seal, and we're prepared to submit that to the registrar and let that be regulated by the registrar in conjunction with my colleague, Ms. Keith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, are you ready to discuss the totality of those documents with the Defence, those under seal, those not under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have engaged in those discussions throughout this litigation. We will be meeting this afternoon -- I hope either this afternoon or tomorrow to have the list available to show to my colleagues from the Defence, and we will reach an agreement that is acceptable to both parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, please, regarding this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon is quite right in saying that we tried to come to an agreement regarding these exhibits, and the methodology that he proposed was accepted by the Defence. So we are waiting for that list, be it today or tomorrow, and then we can agree or come to an agreement as far as that is possible regarding the exhibits to which we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. We're going to wait then before we decide because for us, it was an insurmountable obstacle and we had to encourage your cooperation. I see Mr. Cayley on his feet. Do you have a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I wouldn't dare announce that at this stage, Mr. President. There are some exhibits to be regulated for General Dannatt. Prosecutor's Exhibit 395, 396, 397, 398, and General Dannatt's report which has been marked as Exhibit 385A, which is the English version, and "B" which is the B/C/S version. So if there are no objections from my learned friend Mr. Petrusic, I would ask for those to be admitted into evidence. If I can assist the Defence, they were the biographical documents that were presented at the beginning and then the document showing the relationship between Security Organs within a corps and Divisional Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine then. The documents have been admitted into evidence. That is the decision of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon has asked me to notify the Court that tomorrow there will be two witnesses who will be essentially giving the Court evidence of the impact of these crimes on the community in Srebrenica, and they will be led by Mr. Harmon's legal officer, Magda Karagiannakas, and so she will be leading the evidence tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, once again, to you all for your availability. So we meet again here tomorrow at 9.30. Have a good evening and success in your work.
